turns.speaker: host_a
turns.text: Welcome to the Hearth test bench. Today we are looking at the telemetry from the dual Intel Arc Pro B70 cards after migrating off the AM4 chassis.

turns.speaker: host_b
turns.text: Right. We are clocking 107.8 tokens per second on local Qwen3-30B, but our health checks were flagging the lane as cold.

turns.speaker: host_a
turns.text: Because doorcheck dot py had a boolean defect on line 382. It was inspecting None instead of the live socket state.

turns.speaker: host_b
turns.text: Exactly. Receipts over rhetoric. Per ADR-0014 and ADR-0030, machine control loops must not ride the cloud. The metal is fast, the coordination ledger is durable, and our control loop stays strictly local.

turns.speaker: host_a
turns.text: And when the B70 cards moved to OMEN, summon dot py was still attempting to wake b70-moe dot service on AM4 port 8082.

turns.speaker: host_b
turns.text: The phantom limb problem. Software topology must be audited until every actuator derives its target from declarative pool state.
